samples.summary: `SceneNodeMeta.attrs` is documented as "Attribute names present, sorted", but the new single-source-of-truth reader `attrsOf()` returns names in SOURCE order (`['...', 'id', 'onClick']`, pinned by jsx-nodes.test.mjs:~560). Only `fpOf` sorts, and it sorts a private copy. The extractor that fills `SceneNodeMeta` is the next consumer of `attrsOf`; whichever of the two contracts it follows, the other reader (outline UI vs. fingerprint) is looking at a different ordering than its type says. Either sort in `attrsOf` or fix the type comment before `extract.mjs` lands against it.
samples.evidence: packages/design-editor/src/types.ts:98 `/** Attribute names present, sorted; `...` for a spread. */` vs packages/design-editor/src/server/jsx-nodes.mjs `attrsOf` pushing `names` in iteration order.

samples.summary: `SceneNodeMeta.className` is documented as "`className`'s literal value, or null when it is an expression (`cn(...)`)", but the new `classLiteralOf()` deliberately returns the FIRST string literal inside a `cn(...)` call, and `attrsOf()` surfaces that as `className`. The client type therefore promises `null` exactly where the server now returns a class blob. Any client code that treats a non-null `className` as "this is a plain literal I can safely rewrite whole" will be wrong for `cn()` nodes.
samples.evidence: packages/design-editor/src/types.ts:99 vs packages/design-editor/src/server/jsx-nodes.mjs `classLiteralOf` ('takes the FIRST string literal inside a cn() call', asserted in jsx-nodes.test.mjs).

samples.summary: New second structural guard has no counterpart in the client node model. `resolveNode({requireStatic:true})` now refuses a node when `owner !== node` (a node reached through a `{…}` expression) EVEN IF `scope === 'static'`. The existing client type documents `static` as "directly in the root's returned JSX; all ops allowed", and `structuralEditable` is described as a mirror of the server guard. A client (or the not-yet-written extractor) deriving `structuralEditable` from `scope === 'static'` — which is what this comment tells it to do — will enable a structural op the server now rejects, surfacing as a refused edit after the user has already staged it. The fix belongs on the type comment/extractor: `structuralEditable` must encode owner-ness too.
samples.evidence: packages/design-editor/src/types.ts:113-116 (`'static' — directly in the root's returned JSX; all ops allowed` / `Mirrored server-side as a hard guard in resolveNode`) vs the new `if (hit.owner !== hit.node)` refusal in packages/design-editor/src/server/jsx-nodes.mjs.

samples.summary: The engine design doc's file tree still prescribes `src/server/stamp.d.mts` (plus `inject.d.mts` and `extract.d.mts`) as "Types for the dynamic import". This change deliberately deletes `stamp.d.mts` because an adjacent declaration file SHADOWS the `.mjs` implementation and silently disables its `// @ts-check` (verified in stamp.types.test.mts:16-21). The doc is now the instruction the authors of `inject.mjs` and `extract.mjs` will follow, and following it will re-introduce the exact shadowing bug on the AST MUTATOR — the module that rewrites user source. Nothing catches this: the backticked-path CI check does not recurse into `docs/design/<topic>/`, so this file is unchecked.
samples.evidence: docs/design/design-editor/design-editor-engine.md:85-87 lists `inject.d.mts`, `extract.d.mts`, `stamp.d.mts`; the change removes the `stamp.d.mts` pattern and documents why it is harmful.

samples.summary: `typescript` is a devDependency only, but `src/server/jsx-nodes.mjs` imports it at RUNTIME (`import ts from 'typescript'`), and this package is described as a plugin "installed into a consumer's project" and is explicitly slated for publishing (docs/design/design-editor/design-editor-local-plugin.md:305,338 call `jsx-nodes.mjs` a "stable — published API"). Today it is `private: true` and only `@wafflebase/cli` is published, so nothing breaks now; the moment this package is published, a consumer without TypeScript installed gets a module-not-found at plugin load. `typescript` should move to `dependencies` (or `peerDependencies`) when the package is unprivatised.
samples.evidence: packages/design-editor/package.json:11-15 lists typescript only under devDependencies; packages/design-editor/src/server/jsx-nodes.mjs imports it at module scope.

samples.summary: JSX in ATTRIBUTE position is invisible to all three consumers of this numbering. `childrenOf` only descends into `node.children`, so `<Suspense fallback={<Loader/>}>`, `renderItem={() => <Row/>}` etc. are never numbered, never stamped, and never appear in `SceneMeta`. The doc itself notes `SheetView` has four `<Suspense>` siblings, so this shape is present in the target codebase. Consequence for the DOM→source resolution the host performs (engine doc §7.9/§7.12: nearest ancestor-or-self carrying `data-wb-fp`): clicking a rendered `fallback` element resolves to an ANCESTOR node, i.e. the designer silently selects and edits a different source node than the one clicked — the exact failure the fingerprint scheme exists to prevent. Worth an explicit refusal (or a stamped marker) rather than silent ancestor attribution.
samples.evidence: `childrenOf` returns early unless the node is a JsxElement/JsxFragment and only iterates `node.children`; `attrPropsOf` is used solely for names/identity, never walked for nested JSX. No test in jsx-nodes.test.mjs or stamp.test.mjs covers an attribute-position element.
